title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: DAssemble R package ensemble-based differential association analysis high-throughput omics data. provides flexible framework combining user-specified core method one complementary enhancer methods, allowing users integrate statistical evidence across different modeling assumptions rather relying single differential analysis approach. DAssemble aggregates model-specific p-values using Cauchy Combination Tests (CCT) reports ensemble-level method-specific results. package developed support robust interpretable differential analysis across multiple omics domains, including bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, microbiome data. submitted DAssemble Bioconductor make method easier install, document, test, integrate established Bioconductor workflows data structures, thereby supporting reproducible extensible analysis high-throughput biological data.

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: DAssemble implements ensemble framework differential-abundance differential-expression analysis. Users can choose single core model optionally combine enhancer tests using Cauchy Combination Test. package accepts MultiAssayExperiment object directly. multiple experiments present, use assay_name select experiment analyze. lower-level workflows, features can also data frame samples rows features columns, paired metadata data frame matching sample row names. exposure variable supplied expVar must binary. main DAssemble() function also supports: multiple adjustment covariates coVars repeated-measures / longitudinal designs random_effects open-ended method-specific controls method_args arguments available methods whose wrappers can express corresponding model directly. unsupported methods, DAssemble stops clear error rather fitting mis-specified model.

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: primary entry point : method_args named control list used forward additional arguments underlying methods. argument overlaps DAssemble wrapper default, value method_args takes precedence. usual pattern : method_args$core arguments shared selected core method method_args$enhancer arguments shared selected enhancers method_args$<MethodName> method-specific overrides LR enhancer, wrapper additionally recognizes method_args$LR$separation_method. default "augment", follows MaAsLin3-style augmented logistic fit. cross-sectional presence/absence logistic analyses, users can instead request "firth" use bias-reduced logistic regression brglm2. Maaslin2 core, wrapper also recognizes method_args$Maaslin2$median_comparison = TRUE. requested, DAssemble uses raw fit$results, applies internal median_comparison_tweedie() adjustment , reduces output back standardized exposure-specific result table. Wrappers multi-stage internals can also accept subcall-specific entries. example, method_args$DESeq2 may contain items DESeq, results, estimateSizeFactors, method_args$edgeR may contain items glmFit glmLRT. example, MaAsLin3’s prevalence median comparison can enabled :
code: DAssemble(   features,   metadata = NULL,   core_method = NULL,   enhancers = NULL,   expVar = "group",   coVars = NULL,   random_effects = NULL,   method_args = NULL,   assay_name = NULL,   p_adj = "BY",   enhancer_norm = "TSS",   return_components = TRUE,   return_subensembles = FALSE ) res <- DAssemble(   features = features,   metadata = metadata,   enhancers = "LR",   expVar = "group",   method_args = list(     LR = list(separation_method = "firth")   ) ) res <- DAssemble(   features = features,   metadata = metadata,   core_method = "Maaslin3",   expVar = "group",   method_args = list(     Maaslin3 = list(median_comparison_prevalence = TRUE)   ) )

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: Core methods currently available DAssemble() include: DESeq2 edgeR limmaVOOM metagenomeSeq MAST dearseq ALDEx2 LinDA LOCOM Maaslin2 Maaslin3 Tweedieverse Robseq ANCOMBC2 Enhancers currently available : WLX LR KS

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: current implementation supports multiple covariates (coVars) following methods: random_effects supplied, following methods currently treated longitudinal-compatible: methods treated cross-sectional current package implementation. LR enhancer, default fitting path uses MaAsLin3-style augmentation cross-sectional longitudinal settings. alternative method_args$LR$separation_method = "firth" available non-longitudinal model. Maaslin3 used standard package pathway DAssemble() forced prevalence-mode.

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: airway dataset Bioconductor contains RNA-seq counts airway smooth muscle cells treated dexamethasone. example runs DAssemble DESeq2 core method two enhancers. analysis adjusts cell, combines DESeq2 p-values Wilcoxon logistic-regression enhancer p-values, forwards example control arguments method_args. combined results returned res$res, per-method outputs available res$components.
code: data("airway", package = "airway") counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(airway, "counts") keep_genes <- order(rowSums(counts), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(500L)] counts <- counts[keep_genes, , drop = FALSE] metadata <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(airway)) metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts), , drop = FALSE]  se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(   assays = list(counts = counts) )  mae <- MultiAssayExperiment::MultiAssayExperiment(   experiments = list(rnaseq = se),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(metadata) )  res <- DAssemble::DAssemble(   features = mae,   assay_name = "rnaseq",   core_method = "DESeq2",   enhancers = c("WLX", "LR"),   expVar = "dex",   coVars = "cell",   p_adj = "BH",   enhancer_norm = "tmm",   method_args = list(     DESeq2 = list(       DESeq = list(fitType = "local")     ),     LR = list(       control = glm.control(maxit = 100)     )   ),   return_components = TRUE,   return_subensembles = TRUE ) #> using pre-existing size factors #> estimating dispersions #> gene-wise dispersion estimates #> mean-dispersion relationship #> final dispersion estimates #> fitting model and testing #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes  head(res$res) #>           feature metadata    pval_core   pval_WLX coef_LR pval_LR pval_joint #> 1 ENSG00000115414      dex 9.388328e-01 1.00000000      NA      NA          1 #> 2 ENSG00000011465      dex 1.523315e-03 0.48571429      NA      NA          1 #> 3 ENSG00000198804      dex 8.842089e-01 0.88571429      NA      NA          1 #> 4 ENSG00000156508      dex 4.568638e-04 0.11428571      NA      NA          1 #> 5 ENSG00000164692      dex 1.759305e-08 0.02857143      NA      NA          1 #> 6 ENSG00000116260      dex 2.836045e-01 0.68571429      NA      NA          1 #>   qval #> 1    1 #> 2    1 #> 3    1 #> 4    1 #> 5    1 #> 6    1 names(res$components) #> [1] "DESeq2" "WLX"    "LR"

title: DAssemble: Ensemble Differential Analysis
text: Human Microbiome Project 2 adult example included package shows longitudinal microbiome analysis multiple covariates. feature table metadata stored inst/extdata can accessed installation system.file(). keep vignette build lightweight, evaluated example uses abundant taxa runs Dysbiosis_UC scenario. example also available executable script:

binary_factor(   adult_meta$dysbiosis_state == "dysbiosis_UC" ) adult_meta$dysbiosis_nonIBD <- binary_factor(   adult_meta$dysbiosis_state == "dysbiosis_nonIBD" ) adult_meta$abx_used <- text: methods already combine two models internally (e.g., hurdle two‑part models) /directly output combined p‑value. normally used alone ensemble, .e. core method. Combining hurdle model core methods can double‑count underlying signal lead inflated type error. following methods fall category: Maaslin3 – fits prevalence abundance model hood; MAST – implements hurdle model single‑cell expression data; metagenomeSeq – fits zero‑inflated log‑normal model. may still add enhancers WLX KS models, LR recommended can reintroduce evidence. Combining additional core methods also recommended.

title: Ensemble Models for Differential Analysis
text: main entry point : Key arguments: features – MultiAssayExperiment, data frame samples rows features columns metadata – sample metadata data frame; leave NULL features MultiAssayExperiment expVar – name (column) primary exposure variable (binary, 2 levels) coVars – optional character vector adjustment covariates compatible methods random_effects – optional character vector grouping variables longitudinal-compatible methods method_args – optional named list method-specific control arguments passed selected core method /enhancers assay_name – experiment name use features MultiAssayExperiment; required multiple experiments present core_method – one supported core method names, NULL / "none" run enhancer-analysis enhancers – NULL subset c("WLX", "LR", "KS") p_adj – multiple testing correction method (passed p.adjust) enhancer_norm – normalization used enhancers, one "TSS", "CLR", "TMM", "SCRAN" return_components – TRUE, return per-method results $components return_subensembles – TRUE, compute CCT sub-ensembles return $ensembles main output includes: $res – data frame features ranked joint CCT p-value adjusted q-value $components – named list individual core/enhancer result tables (returned default) $ensembles – (optional) table sub-ensemble CCT results example, core_method = "DESeq2" enhancers = c("WLX", "LR"), individual results available result$components$DESeq2, result$components$WLX, result$components$LR. tables alter joint ranking result$res.
code: DAssemble(   features,   metadata      = NULL,   core_method   = NULL,   enhancers     = NULL,   expVar        = "group",   coVars        = NULL,   random_effects = NULL,   method_args   = NULL,   assay_name    = NULL,   p_adj         = "BY",   enhancer_norm = "TSS",   return_components   = TRUE,   return_subensembles = FALSE )

title: Ensemble Models for Differential Analysis
text: DAssemble() supports open-ended method_args control list users can pass additional arguments underlying methods without package needing enumerate every possible option top-level API. argument overlaps DAssemble wrapper default, value method_args takes precedence. expected pattern : method_args$core arguments shared selected core method method_args$enhancer arguments shared requested enhancers method_args$<MethodName> method-specific overrides method_args$Maaslin3 method_args$LR LR enhancer specifically, wrapper also recognizes method_args$LR$separation_method. default "augment", follows MaAsLin3-style augmented logistic fit. cross-sectional presence/absence logistic models, users can instead request "firth" use bias-reduced logistic regression via brglm2. Maaslin2 core, wrapper also recognizes method_args$Maaslin2$median_comparison = TRUE. requested, DAssemble uses raw fit$results, applies internal median_comparison_tweedie() adjustment , reduces output back standardized exposure-specific result table. wrappers multiple internal stages, method_args$<MethodName> can also target subcalls. example, DESeq2 wrapper can receive entries DESeq, results, estimateSizeFactors, edgeR wrapper can receive entries glmFit glmLRT. Example: example, MaAsLin3’s prevalence median comparison can enabled retaining DAssemble defaults:
code: res <- DAssemble(   features = features,   metadata = metadata,   enhancers = "LR",   expVar = "group",   method_args = list(     LR = list(separation_method = "firth")   ) ) res <- DAssemble(   features = features,   metadata = metadata,   core_method = "Maaslin3",   expVar = "group",   method_args = list(     Maaslin3 = list(median_comparison_prevalence = TRUE)   ) )

WLX alone, LR alone, KS alone WLX + LR, WLX + KS, LR + KS WLX + LR + KS resulting $ensembles object, sub_ensemble (similarly named) column labels combination (e.g., "WLX", "WLX+LR", "LR+KS", "WLX+LR+KS"). useful sensitivity analysis: can see conclusions change move individual tests different CCT combinations, including enhancer-setting core method used.

title: Ensemble Models for Differential Analysis
text: airway dataset Bioconductor package airway small RNA‑Seq experiment four airway smooth muscle cell lines treated asthma medication dexamethasone. often used introductory example differential expression analysis; dataset comprises counts ~63 k genes measured eight samples (4 × 2 design). Bioconductor vignette notes airway dataset provides typical small‑scale RNA‑Seq experiment four ASM cell lines treated dexamethasone. run DAssemble dataset using DESeq2 core two enhancers (Wilcoxon logistic regression): call normalizes counts using TMM scheme (enhancer_norm = "tmm"), adjusts cell albut, combines DESeq2 Wilcoxon logistic regression enhancers, returns full set sub‑ensembles. can access individual method outputs $components element result. method_args list illustrates forward extra options underlying DESeq2 logistic-regression wrappers.
code: library(DESeq2) library(airway) library(MultiAssayExperiment) library(DAssemble)  # load counts and metadata data("airway") counts   <- assay(airway, "counts") metadata <- as.data.frame(colData(airway)) metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts), , drop = FALSE]  mae <- MultiAssayExperiment(   experiments = list(rnaseq = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(     assays = list(counts = counts)   )),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(metadata) )  # the exposure variable is dex (treated vs untreated) res <- DAssemble(   features    = mae,   assay_name  = "rnaseq",   core_method = "DESeq2",   enhancers   = c("WLX", "LR"),   expVar      = "dex",   coVars      = c("cell", "albut"),   p_adj       = "BH",   enhancer_norm = "tmm",   method_args = list(     DESeq2 = list(       DESeq = list(fitType = "local")     ),     LR = list(       control = glm.control(maxit = 100)     )   ),   return_components = TRUE,   return_subensembles = TRUE )  # inspect the top differential genes head(res$res) # inspect per‑method p‑values names(res$components)

title: Ensemble Models for Differential Analysis
text: Global Patterns dataset, available via phyloseq package, contains 16S rRNA profiles 25 environmental samples three synthetic “mock communities,” representing nine sample types total average sequencing depth 3.1 million reads per sample【156744987103578†L128-L133】. used explore diversity patterns across variety ecosystems. run enhancer‑DAssemble analysis microbiome count table extracted GlobalPatterns: example core set NULL, analysis combines three nonparametric enhancers . microbiome data compositional, use centered log‑ratio (CLR) normalization (enhancer_norm = "clr"). $components element contains individual Wilcoxon, logistic regression KS results, $ensembles summarises every sub‑combination three enhancers.
code: library(phyloseq) library(MultiAssayExperiment) library(DAssemble)  # load Global Patterns as a phyloseq object data("GlobalPatterns") gp <- GlobalPatterns  # extract count matrix and sample metadata otu  <- as(otu_table(gp), "matrix") meta <- as.data.frame(sample_data(gp))  # here we compare human fecal samples against soil samples as an example keep <- meta$SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Soil") X    <- t(otu[, keep]) meta <- meta[keep, , drop = FALSE] meta$group <- droplevels(factor(meta$SampleType)) stopifnot(nlevels(meta$group) == 2L)  mae <- MultiAssayExperiment(   experiments = list(microbiome = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(     assays = list(counts = t(as.matrix(X)))   )),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(meta) )  res <- DAssemble(   features    = mae,   assay_name  = "microbiome",   core_method = NULL,   enhancers   = c("WLX", "LR", "KS"),   expVar      = "group",   enhancer_norm = "clr",   return_components = TRUE,   return_subensembles = TRUE )  head(res$res)
